options.text: A type of mutation in DNA
The differences that exist between individuals of the same species
The inheritance of characteristics from parents

questions.explanation: Variation refers to the differences that exist between individuals of the same species. No two individuals are exactly alike, and this variation provides the raw material for natural selection and evolution.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of environmental variation?
questions.explanation: A scar from an injury is caused entirely by the environment, not by genes. Blood group, natural hair colour, and tongue rolling are all examples of genetic variation.

questions.stem: What is the difference between continuous and discontinuous variation?

options.text: Continuous variation is genetic; discontinuous is environmental
Continuous variation shows a range of phenotypes; discontinuous has distinct categories
Continuous variation only occurs in plants; discontinuous only in animals
There is no difference; they are the same thing

questions.explanation: Continuous variation shows a range of phenotypes with no distinct categories (e.g., height, mass), while discontinuous variation has distinct, separate categories with no intermediates (e.g., blood group, tongue rolling).

questions.stem: Which of the following is a source of genetic variation?
questions.explanation: Meiosis (through crossing over and independent assortment) and random fertilisation are key sources of genetic variation. Diet, exercise, and climate are environmental factors that cause environmental variation.

questions.stem: Height in humans is an example of variation caused by:

options.text: A combination of genetic and environmental factors

questions.explanation: Height is influenced by both genetic factors (genes inherited from parents) and environmental factors (such as nutrition during childhood). Most characteristics are affected by a combination of both.

questions.stem: Which type of variation is shown on a bar chart with distinct categories?
questions.explanation: Discontinuous variation is shown on a bar chart because individuals fall into distinct categories (e.g., blood group A, B, AB, or O). Continuous variation is shown on a bell-shaped histogram because there is a range of values.

questions.stem: Why is variation important for a species?

options.text: It ensures all individuals look the same
It increases the chance that some individuals will survive environmental changes
It guarantees that all offspring will survive

questions.explanation: Variation is important because it increases the chance that some individuals in a population will have characteristics suited to surviving environmental changes. Without variation, an entire population could be wiped out by a single change.
